pr.title: Correctly compute adjustment casts in GVN
pr.author: cjgillot

processing.reason: The PR does not describe a value-level miscompilation; it fixes a compiler ICE. In the historical GVN code, `CastKind::PointerCoercion(UnsafeFnPointer | MutToConstPointer | ArrayToPointer)` was routed through `InterpCx::ptr_to_ptr`. For the regression case (`fn(i32, i32)` coerced to `unsafe fn(i32, i32)`), `ptr_to_ptr` asserts that the destination type is an unsafe raw pointer (`assert!(cast_to.ty.is_unsafe_ptr())`), which fails before any value is produced. The corrected code uses `ImmTy::from_immediate`, i.e. a no-op reinterpretation, so the observable runtime value (the function pointer) is unchanged. The historical test contains no expected value difference and is marked `// skip-filecheck`; its stated purpose is only: “Verify that we do not ICE when attempting to interpret casts between fn types.” Therefore there is no source-grounded pair of defined Rust executions whose original and transformed values differ. Modeling the old path as a panic/sentinel or as an arbitrary pointer transformation would manufacture behavior not present in the historical transformation, and the required Miri-validated differing-value counterexample cannot be constructed honestly.

analysis.summary: GVN's cast evaluation incorrectly routed PointerCoercion adjustment casts (including UnsafeFnPointer) through const-eval ptr_to_ptr, causing an ICE on casts between fn types. The fix splits FnPtrToPtr/PtrToPtr (which still use ptr_to_ptr) from MutToConstPointer/ArrayToPointer/UnsafeFnPointer adjustment coercions, which now reinterpret the immediate with ImmTy::from_immediate.
analysis.originalLogic: In VnState's cast handling, one match arm covered all of `CastKind::FnPtrToPtr`, `CastKind::PtrToPtr`, and `CastKind::PointerCoercion(MutToConstPointer | ArrayToPointer | UnsafeFnPointer)`. For every such cast it read the source immediate, computed the target layout, and called `self.ecx.ptr_to_ptr(&src, to)`: "let ret = self.ecx.ptr_to_ptr(&src, to).ok()?; ret.into()".
analysis.incorrectTransformation: For an adjustment cast represented as `CastKind::PointerCoercion(...)`, especially `PointerCoercion::UnsafeFnPointer` between function-pointer types, GVN treated the adjustment like a pointer-to-pointer cast and invoked `ptr_to_ptr`. This is the historically incorrect transformation: interpreting these adjustment casts via `ptr_to_ptr` is wrong and ICEs when "attempting to interpret casts between fn types." The corrected behavior keeps `FnPtrToPtr | PtrToPtr` on `ptr_to_ptr`, but for the adjustment-coercion arm replaces the call with `ImmTy::from_immediate(*src, to).into()`.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR bodies containing cast Rvalues whose `CastKind` is `PointerCoercion::UnsafeFnPointer`, `MutToConstPointer`, or `ArrayToPointer`, and pointer casts `FnPtrToPtr`/`PtrToPtr`. The regression input domain specifically includes a safe function pointer assigned to an unsafe function pointer, e.g. `static BAR: fn(i32, i32) = |a, b| assert_ne!(a, b);` followed by `let bar: unsafe fn(i32, i32) = BAR;`, plus repeated calls through function-pointer locals so GVN processes/deduplicates those values.
analysis.trigger: GVN reaches its cast-evaluation logic for a `CastKind::PointerCoercion` adjustment cast, particularly `UnsafeFnPointer` whose source and destination are function-pointer types. Under the old combined match arm it calls `ecx.ptr_to_ptr` on that function-pointer immediate/target layout, producing an ICE rather than a correct value-numbering result.
preconditions: The GVN MIR optimization pass is enabled and attempts to evaluate the cast Rvalue.
The MIR contains a cast with CastKind::PointerCoercion among MutToConstPointer, ArrayToPointer, or UnsafeFnPointer.
For the fn-type regression, the source and destination are function-pointer types, e.g. fn(i32, i32) coerced to unsafe fn(i32, i32).
The source immediate and destination layout are obtainable, so execution reaches the ptr_to_ptr call.
pitfalls: Do not treat all casts in the original match arm as equivalent: FnPtrToPtr and PtrToPtr legitimately still use ptr_to_ptr, while adjustment PointerCoercion casts must reinterpret the immediate via ImmTy::from_immediate.
Do not generalize the fix to replace ptr_to_ptr for PtrToPtr/FnPtrToPtr; that would change pointer-cast evaluation semantics rather than merely fixing adjustment handling.
Do not conflate an unsafe-fn-pointer coercion (PointerCoercion::UnsafeFnPointer) with a raw pointer-to-pointer cast (FnPtrToPtr/PtrToPtr).
The supplied evidence is source and test text only; no compiler was built, so do not claim the ICE was reproduced or that the test was executed.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a `tests/mir-opt` regression test (the historical test has `// skip-filecheck`) containing static function items and an unsafe-fn-pointer coercion, e.g. assign `fn(i32, i32)` to `unsafe fn(i32, i32)`, plus repeated calls through `fn()` and `fn(i32)` locals to exercise GVN value numbering. Compile the same input under the old combined-arm logic versus the corrected split logic and verify the old `ptr_to_ptr` path is what changes: the fixed version must compile without ICE while still using `ptr_to_ptr` for FnPtrToPtr/PtrToPtr. Test text explicitly states the goal: "Verify that we do not ICE when attempting to interpret casts between fn types."
